new_leaves.label: Spatialism
new_leaves.defn: Movement founded by Lucio Fontana in Milan in 1947 (anticipated by the Manifiesto blanco, Buenos Aires 1946) that sought to fuse colour, sound, space, movement and time, projecting art into real space with neon, television and the slashed and punctured canvas (Buchi, Tagli).

new_leaves.defn: The first post-war avant-garde group in Spain, founded in Barcelona in 1948 by Joan Brossa with Antoni Tàpies, Modest Cuixart, Joan Ponç and others, drawing on Surrealism and Dada and publishing the review Dau al Set until 1956.

new_leaves.label: Supports/Surfaces
new_leaves.defn: French group of 1966–1972 from Montpellier, Nîmes and Nice that deconstructed painting into its support (stretcher) and surface (canvas): unstretched canvases, stretchers without canvas and repeated imprinted forms, with a Marxist and structuralist theory.

new_leaves.label: Synchromism
new_leaves.defn: American colour abstraction founded in Paris in 1912–1913 by Morgan Russell and Stanton Macdonald-Wright, orchestrating colour on the analogy of music (synchromies); the first American avant-garde movement to receive international attention.

new_leaves.defn: Naturalistic painting of everyday American life of the 1920s–1940s, rooted in the Ashcan School and encouraged by the federal art projects of the Depression, comprising the Regionalists (Benton, Wood, Curry) and the Social Realists.

new_leaves.defn: Group of young Paris painters (1888–c. 1900) formed around Paul Sérusier's Talisman, painted under Gauguin's guidance at Pont-Aven: Bonnard, Vuillard, Denis, Ranson, Vallotton; flat colour, decorative pattern and intimate interiors, with screens, posters and theatre design.
